Chapter 11. Diagnostics and Troubleshooting

Source: vignettes/articles/11-Diagnostics-and-Troubleshooting.Rmd
11-Diagnostics-and-Troubleshooting.Rmd

Decant reports when its estimate is uncertain. This chapter explains each message and what to do about it.

11.1 Three checks after every run 

library(Decant)
sim <- simulate_experiment(seed = 1)
res <- decant(sim$observed, sim$empty, clusters = sim$labels)

quantile(res$rho, c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9))
#>       10%       50%       90% 
#> 0.1167786 0.1993348 0.3052685 
res$soup_mismatch
#> [1] FALSE
any(res$rho_diagnostics$low_power)
#> [1] FALSE
  1. Is rho plausible? Single-cell data typically show 0.02 to 0.10 and single-nucleus data up to 0.30. A median far outside this range deserves a closer look.
  2. soup_mismatch should be FALSE.
  3. low_power should be FALSE for all clusters, or at least for the large ones.

11.2 Warning: soup/cell mismatch

X% of the soup is in N gene(s) the cells do not contain … rho is UNDERestimated.

Meaning. A noticeable share of the soup (more than 5%) is in genes that no cell expresses. The empty droplets contain material that is not ambient RNA from these cells, for example debris, red blood cells, or a cell type that was removed by filtering.

What Decant does. It removes those genes from the soup before estimating rho.

What to do. - Look at the top soup genes: head(sort(res$ambient[, 1], decreasing = TRUE), 20). - If they belong to a cell type you filtered out, consider keeping those cells. - If rho still looks too low, supply an independent estimate with rho = ... (Chapter 5.6).

11.3 Warning: low-power clusters

N cluster(s) have almost no genes that are cleanly absent, so rho is weakly identified there and likely OVERestimated.

Meaning. In these clusters almost every gene in the soup is also expressed, so there is little evidence about the soup alone. This happens with very small clusters and with cell types whose expression resembles the soup.

What Decant does. It gives these clusters the rho of the other clusters, weighted by their evidence (borrowed = TRUE in res$rho_diagnostics).

What to do. Merge very small clusters, or cluster at a lower resolution, and run again.

11.4 Common errors

Message Cause Fix
empties needs nrow(obs_total) genes Cells and empty droplets have different genes Create both with split_droplets() from the same raw matrix
length(clusters) must equal ncol(obs_total) The cluster vector does not match the cells Use one label per cell, in column order
`sample_of` is required when `empties` is a list Several soups but no sample assignment Pass sample_of (Chapter 8)
need at least 2 cells Too few cells Check the cell filtering
RunDecant() refuses the object The assay holds normalised or SCTransformed values Use the assay with raw UMI counts (assay = "RNA")

11.5 Frequently asked questions

Do I need the raw matrix? It is strongly recommended, because the empty droplets measure the soup. With filtered data only, you can approximate the soup by the pooled expression of all cells, as SoupX does in the same situation:

pooled <- Matrix::Matrix(Matrix::rowSums(sim$observed), ncol = 1, sparse = TRUE,
                         dimnames = list(rownames(sim$observed), "pooled"))
res_pooled <- decant(sim$observed, pooled, clusters = sim$labels)
  • pooled is a one-column matrix holding the summed counts of all cells. Decant treats it as a single, very deep empty droplet.
  • This soup is biased towards the abundant cell types, so treat the result as approximate.

How many empty droplets do I need? The soup should rest on at least about 50,000 UMIs (soup_umis in the split_droplets() summary). A standard 10x run has far more.

Should I correct before or after quality control? Remove empty and damaged barcodes first (cell calling), then run Decant, then do the rest of the analysis (normalisation, clustering, markers) on the corrected counts.

Can I use Decant with single-nucleus data? Yes. Contamination is usually higher, which makes correction more important. For velocity, see Chapter 10.

Why are some counts still present for marker genes in the wrong cell type? Decant removes what ambient RNA can explain. Counts far above that level, often from doublets, are left in place on purpose: they are not ambient RNA and should be handled by doublet detection.
